provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Review of JSS2 Work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall basic programming concepts.
The students should be able to list components of a simple robot.
Introduction:
We have learned about programming and robotics in JSS2. Today we will revise these topics to build a strong foundation.
Content:
Programming involves writing instructions for computers using languages like Python or Scratch. We can use programming to create simple games or solve problems. Robotics combines mechanics and electronics to build machines that can perform tasks. For example, we can build a robot that sorts objects by color.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to create a simple flowchart for a sorting algorithm.
Evaluation questions:
What is programming?
Name two programming languages you know.
What is a robot?
How can programming be used in everyday life?
Summary:
Today we reviewed programming and robotics concepts that we learned in JSS2.

topics.title: Advanced MS Word
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create properly formatted documents with tables.
The students should be able to perform mail merge operations.
Introduction:
We have used MS Word for basic writing tasks. Today we will learn advanced features to create professional documents.
Content:
Page layout includes setting margins, headers, footers and page numbers. Tables help organize information neatly in rows and columns. Mail merge allows us to personalize letters by combining a main document with a data source. For example, we can send personalized invitation letters to all parents of students.
Class activity:
Students will create a newsletter with multiple columns, images and a table of events.
Evaluation questions:
What is page layout?
How do you insert a table in MS Word?
What is mail merge?
Name one use of mail merge in school.
Summary:
Today we learned advanced MS Word features like page layout, tables and mail merge.

topics.title: Advanced MS PowerPoint
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to apply animations and transitions to slides.
The students should be able to integrate multimedia elements into presentations.
Introduction:
We have created basic presentations in MS PowerPoint. Today we will learn to make our presentations more engaging with animations and multimedia.
Content:
Animations make objects on slides move or appear in special ways. Transitions control how slides change from one to another. Multimedia integration means adding videos, audio clips and images to presentations. For example, we can add a short video of a science experiment to explain a concept better.
Class activity:
Students will create a presentation about Nigerian culture with at least three animations and two transitions.
Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between animation and transition?
How do you add a video to a PowerPoint slide?
Name two types of multimedia you can use in presentations.
Why are animations important in presentations?
Summary:
Today we learned to enhance presentations with animations, transitions and multimedia elements.

topics.title: Introduction to Digital Media
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define digital media.
The students should be able to explain the importance of digital media.
The students should be able to create simple digital content.
Introduction:
We use digital media every day on our phones and computers. Today we will learn what digital media is and how to create it.
Content:
Digital media refers to content that is stored in digital format. It includes text, images, audio and video. Digital media is important because it allows us to share information quickly and reach many people. Creating digital content involves using tools like cameras, microphones and software to produce media. For example, we can create a digital poster about our school using Canva.
Class activity:
Students will create a simple digital poster about their favorite Nigerian food using Canva.
Evaluation questions:
What is digital media?
Name three types of digital media.
Why is digital media important?
What tools can we use to create digital content?
Summary:
Today we learned about digital media and how to create simple digital content.

topics.title: MID-TERM TEST
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of topics covered in Weeks 1-4.
Introduction:
We have learned about programming, advanced MS Word, PowerPoint and digital media. Today we will test our understanding of these topics.
Content:
The test will cover the following topics: Review of JSS2 programming and robotics, advanced MS Word features including page layout, tables and mail merge, advanced PowerPoint features including animations and multimedia integration, and introduction to digital media including its meaning, importance and creation.
Class activity:
Students will complete a written test covering all topics from Weeks 1-4.
Evaluation questions:
The test will consist of multiple choice, short answer and practical questions.
Summary:
Today we assessed our understanding of the topics covered in the first four weeks of term.

topics.title: Graphic Design with Canva
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create posters using Canva.
The students should be able to design flyers and social media posts.
Introduction:
We have seen digital media examples. Today we will learn to create our own designs using Canva, a popular graphic design tool.
Content:
Canva is an online tool that allows us to create designs easily. Posters are large designs used to advertise events or share information. Flyers are smaller papers that give details about an event. Social media posts are designed for platforms like Instagram or Facebook. For example, we can design a poster for our school's cultural day celebration.
Class activity:
Students will create a set of designs for a school event including a poster, flyer and social media post.
Evaluation questions:
What is Canva?
Name three types of designs you can create with Canva.
What is the difference between a poster and a flyer?
Why is good design important for social media posts?
Summary:
Today we learned to create various designs using Canva.

topics.title: MID-TERM BREAK
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to rest and prepare for the second half of the term.
Introduction:
We have completed six weeks of learning. It is time to rest and recharge our minds.
Content:
This is a holiday period where students rest and spend time with family. It is important to take breaks from studying to stay healthy and focused. During this break, you can review what you have learned so far and prepare for new topics.
Class activity:
No formal class activity during the break. Students are encouraged to rest and engage in recreational activities.
Evaluation questions:
No formal evaluation during the break.
Summary:
Enjoy your break and come back refreshed for more learning.

topics.title: Photo Editing and Visual Communication Usi
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to edit photos using online tools.
The students should be able to explain how visual communication works.
Introduction:
We have created designs. Today we will learn to edit photos and use them for visual communication.
Content:
Photo editing involves changing or enhancing digital photographs. Online tools like Pixlr or Photopea allow us to edit photos without installing software. Visual communication uses images to convey messages effectively. For example, we can edit a photo of our school to make it look more attractive for a brochure.
Class activity:
Students will edit a photo of their choice using an online photo editing tool and write a short paragraph explaining how it communicates a message.
Evaluation questions:
What is photo editing?
Name two online tools for photo editing.
What is visual communication?
How can edited photos be used in branding?
Summary:
Today we learned about photo editing and visual communication using online tools.

topics.title: Copyright and Media Ethics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain copyright laws.
The students should be able to identify ethical issues in digital media.
Introduction:
We create and use digital content. It is important to understand how to use content legally and ethically.
Content:
Copyright is legal protection for original works like music, photos and videos. It gives creators rights to control how their work is used. Fair use allows limited use of copyrighted material without permission for purposes like education or criticism. Media ethics involves making good choices about creating and sharing content. For example, we should always credit the source of images we use in our projects.
Class activity:
Students will analyze case studies of copyright violations and discuss ethical solutions.
Evaluation questions:
What is copyright?
What is fair use?
Why is it important to respect copyright?
Name one ethical issue in digital media.
Summary:
Today we learned about copyright laws and media ethics in digital media.

topics.title: Digital Portfolio Creation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to create a digital portfolio.
The students should be able to organize digital works effectively.
Introduction:
We have created various digital works throughout the term. Today we will learn to compile them into a digital portfolio.
Content:
A digital portfolio is a collection of digital work that showcases our skills and achievements. It can include documents, presentations, photos and videos. Creating a portfolio helps us organize our work and demonstrate our abilities to others. For example, we can create a portfolio of all our Canva designs and PowerPoint presentations from this term.
Class activity:
Students will create a digital portfolio using Google Sites or a similar platform, organizing their best works from the term.
Evaluation questions:
What is a digital portfolio?
Name three types of content that can be in a digital portfolio.
Why is a portfolio useful?
How can you organize your portfolio effectively?
Summary:
Today we learned how to create and organize a digital portfolio of our works.

topics.title: REVISION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to recall all topics covered in the term.
The students should be able to demonstrate understanding of key concepts.
Introduction:
We have covered many topics this term. Today we will revise all the important concepts to prepare for our examination.
Content:
We will review the following topics: programming and robotics, advanced MS Word features, PowerPoint animations and multimedia, digital media, graphic design with Canva, photo editing, copyright and media ethics, and digital portfolio creation. We will focus on key concepts and practical applications of each topic.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create revision flashcards for different topics and quiz each other.
Evaluation questions:
What is mail merge?
How do you add animations in PowerPoint?
What is copyright?
Why are digital portfolios important?
Summary:
Today we revised all the important topics from the term to prepare for our examination.

topics.title: EXAMINATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to demonstrate knowledge of all topics covered in the term.
Introduction:
We have completed our revision. Today we will take our end of term examination to assess our learning.
Content:
The examination will cover all topics from the term including programming, advanced MS Word, PowerPoint, digital media, graphic design, photo editing, copyright and digital portfolios. It will include theoretical questions and practical tasks to demonstrate our skills.
Class activity:
Students will complete the end of term examination covering all topics from the term.
Evaluation questions:
The examination will consist of multiple choice, short answer and practical questions.
Summary:
Today we completed our end of term examination to assess our learning.

topics.title: CLOSING/VACATION
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to reflect on their learning throughout the term.
Introduction:
We have completed all our lessons and examinations for the term. Today we will close the term and prepare for vacation.
Content:
This is the final week of the term where we reflect on what we have learned and achieved. Students will receive their results and feedback on their performance. It is important to celebrate our successes and identify areas for improvement in the next term.
Class activity:
Students will complete a reflection worksheet about their learning experience and share their favorite project from the term.
Evaluation questions:
What was your favorite topic this term?
What skills have you improved?
What would you like to learn next term?
Summary:
Today we closed the term and reflected on our learning achievements.
